tier_reason: astral4/fft-benchmark (5 stars, not a well-known suite, so not B) publishes code (benches/fftw.rs, benches/rustfft.rs), rustc/clang versions and an M1 CPU, but its FFTW baseline is handicapped: the fftw crate's default 'source' feature builds FFTW 3.3.8 via fftw-src with './configure --with-pic --enable-static --disable-doc' (no --enable-neon, so scalar codelets), and every timed iteration creates a fresh FFTW_ESTIMATE plan. Treated like a de-optimised baseline (cap at C); even so RustFFT loses at several sizes.

corrections.baseline: FFTW 3.3.8 (via the Rust fftw crate v0.8.0, built from source by fftw-src without any SIMD configure flag, FFTW_ESTIMATE plan created inside each timed call)
corrections.claimed_speedup: Table medians, forward / inverse, plan creation included in the timed region for both libraries. f32 N=8,388,608: RustFFT 103.9 / 103.6 ms vs FFTW 193.3 / 192.9 ms (about 1.86x, derived from page data); f32 N=16: 124.6 / 94.09 ns vs 1.405 / 1.416 us; f32 N=1,048,576: 12.49 / 12.58 ms vs 14.20 / 13.13 ms (about 1.14x forward, derived from page data); f64 N=65,536: 754.4 / 774.5 us vs 953.5 / 966.9 us (about 1.26x forward, derived from page data). RustFFT is SLOWER than this FFTW build at f32 N=1024 (7.707 vs 7.291 us), N=2048 (22.87 vs 11.74 us, FFTW about 1.95x faster, derived from page data), N=4096 (45.33 vs 21.20 us), N=8192 forward (84.08 vs 45.62 us), N=16384 both directions (156.7 / 225.2 vs 101.1 / 180.0 us), and at f64 N=1024 (8.624 vs 7.749 us), N=2048 (18.49 vs 12.54 us) and N=524,288 (9.427 vs 7.911 ms). The author's conclusion 'fftw was consistently slower than both rustfft and phastft' is contradicted by the page's own table for RustFFT.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: rustc 1.80.0-nightly (d2d24e395 2024-05-03); Cargo.toml [profile.bench] lto = true, strip = true (cargo bench default opt-level 3), no target-cpu or RUSTFLAGS stated; rustfft v6.2.0; fftw crate v0.8.0 default 'source' feature: fftw-src build.rs runs FFTW 3.3.8 './configure --with-pic --enable-static --disable-doc' (plus --enable-single for f32), no SIMD flag, compiled with Apple clang 15.0.0 (clang-1500.0.40.1)
corrections.workload: Single-threaded in-place complex-to-complex forward and inverse FFT, f32 and f64, power-of-two lengths 8 to 8,388,608, divan medians, in the third-party astral4/fft-benchmark on an M1 MacBook Pro. Each timed call includes planning: FFTW builds a C2CPlan with FFTW_ESTIMATE | DESTROYINPUT and executes it; RustFFT calls plan_fft_forward/inverse on a fresh FftPlanner (created in untimed setup) and processes.
corrections.caveats: Third-party, single-machine, Apple Silicon only, small repo (5 stars). The FFTW baseline is handicapped: built by the fftw-src crate with no --enable-neon (scalar codelets), planned with FFTW_ESTIMATE, and planning is timed on every call, which explains FFTW's ~1.4 us at N=8 to 32; so the results do not show RustFFT beating a SIMD-enabled, pre-planned FFTW. Even against this build RustFFT is slower at f32 N=1024 to 16384 and f64 N=1024, 2048 and 524,288. The ejmahler/RustFFT README and release notes state no benchmark numbers against FFTW (the 'now faster than FFTW' claim is a 2020 Rust forum post for 5.0.0-experimental.1 that could not be opened from this container). Pure Rust with no C ABI, so not callable from C++ without writing an FFI layer.

notes: Numbers match the astral4 README table exactly, but the comparison is against a scalar FFTW 3.3.8 with plan creation timed, and the record understated where RustFFT loses. Scope flag: Rust-only library (no C API); orchestrator may want to file it as a non-C++ entry. Metadata confirmed: MIT OR Apache-2.0, 942 stars, last commit 2026-09-29, not a fork.

tier_reason: First-party gnuplot SVG (docs/speed.svg) compares minfft with KissFFT, PocketFFT and 'fftw sse2'; the repo ships no benchmark code and states no CPU, compiler or flags, so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README says its speed and accuracy are compared with 'the libraries of similar design - KissFFT and PocketFFT', with 'a highly optimized machine-specific version of the FFTW library' shown for reference; the plot has no numbers in text. Digitised from docs/speed.svg point coordinates (derived from page data, approximate; axes log2(N) 1-20 and Mflops): minfft is above KissFFT at every size, 1.36x to 4.83x, median about 1.96x (N=2^10: about 8,200 vs 5,000 Mflops). Versus PocketFFT minfft is faster only at N<=2^6 and N=2^17 to 2^18 and about 0.74x to 0.96x elsewhere (median about 0.92x). Versus 'fftw sse2' about 0.34x to 0.89x (median about 0.56x).

notes: My own digitisation of the SVG path data reproduces the record's ratios. Faster than KissFFT (a listed fft baseline), not faster than FFTW or PocketFFT at most sizes. Metadata confirmed: MIT, 53 stars, not a fork, last commit 2025-08-11 (stale); repo root holds only minfft.c/.h/.F03, docs and LICENSE, no bench code.

tier_reason: No opened page has OTFFT timings: the DEWETRON README, the kfrlib/fft-benchmark README (OTFFT 11.5.0 is a supported library but no results are published in the repo) and the temerkhanov/OTFFT mirror (ships fftbench0-3.cpp and cpp_fftw3.h, no results) all lack numbers; the upstream homepage is egress-blocked.

corrections.caveats: No numeric evidence was opened, so this is tier D. A WebSearch snippet (not opened) says the upstream homepage wwwa.pikara.ne.jp/okojisan/otfft-en/ claims OTFFT is faster than FFTW at lengths 2^1 to 2^24, measured on a Surface Laptop 5 with GCC 11.4.0, OTFFT 11.6 and FFTW 3.3.10; a verifier that can open that page should re-tier. Upstream benchmark code exists (fftbench*.cpp with cpp_fftw3.h, mirrored in temerkhanov/OTFFT) but results are only on the homepage. The DEWETRON repo is a source-level fork of OK Ojisan's (Takuya Okahisa) upstream, synced to version 11.5, not a GitHub fork; last commit 2022-08-17. kfrlib/fft-benchmark lists it as double precision only and x86 only; upstream builds target the compiling machine's ISA (an AVX build crashes on CPUs without AVX, per the akinomyoga/OTFFT README).
